newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end sharply off on Dow jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end sharply off on Dow jitters.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell sharply Wednesday following the drop in the Dow Jones industrial average and on a lack of foreign investor interest and sales of stocks by local investors ahead of Thursday's holiday.
"The bourse was very weak. New York hurt us most as it made local and foreign investors nervous," said Daniel Romo, research chief at the Bancrecer bank.
The blue chip IPC index ended off 65.31 points, or 1.98 percent, at 3,241.75. points.
The Dow fell 70.73 points, or 1.09 percent, at 6,402.52 points. Analysts said both the Dow and Mexican stocks began to slide following a steep drop in U.S. Treasury bonds.
Some traders put the late slide down to dealers selling stocks to stay liquid over the national Virgin of Guadalupe holiday on Thursday.
"No one knows what the Dow Jones will do tomorrow, so some preferred to go liquid and step out," said one trader.
On the broad market, 96 stocks changed hands as losers trounced gainers by 72 to six.
One notable gainer was steelmaker Grupo IMSA, which concluded an Initial Public Offering Wednesday. IMSA closed at 17.00 pesos ($2.15), or 37 centavos (5 cents) above its issue price.
Debt-stricken holding group Sidek headed the losers after closing down 11 centavos (1 cent) at 71 centavos (9 cents).
